summary:
I worked only from the benchmark's published traces (T03 gptr 1.0.1 at commit 5e2992b, and T01/T08 with gptr 1.0.0). In T03 the median wall time was 244.46 s for A1 (gptr) and 226.30 s for C1 (Codex), with 3-4 versus 19-28 tool calls. Nearly all of A1's extra time is gptr's own in-process time, not the model.

1. **Gap around each r call.** The gap is the outer interval minus the internal elapsed time. It is 2.1-2.3 s in request 1. In requests 2 and 3 it is 28.3-36.0 s in A1-2 and A1-3, and 55.3-57.1 s in A1-1, which is 88-96% of each call. Per run that totals 59.4-114.9 s (median 68.1 s). C1's matching cost is 0.63-0.78 s per Rscript (median 0.67 s) for launch and exit, plus 2.5-3.7 s per run of Codex wrapper time outside R.
2. **The "harness/model/network" excess is not the model.** The benchmark reports A1 +29.15 s on the mean. A1's time inside the Codex CLI provider, net of tool calls, is 74-82 s per run, no more than C1's model/harness time of 74-86 s. The excess is gptr time outside the provider:
   - 15.1-29.4 s after the provider returns in request 1 (0.7-1.3 s in requests 2 and 3), against C1's 0.02 s;
   - 0.9-3.4 s before each provider start, 6.2-6.6 s per run;
   - 4.5 s more startup and cleanup outside the requests.
3. **The cost tracks large bindings.** A1-1's code never ran `rm(tables)`, so the dead fallback branch assigned two 5 GB bindings (`tables` and `raw`) instead of one. Its request-2/3 gaps (57.1 and 55.3 s) and its request-1 post-provider time (29.4 s) are about twice A1-2/A1-3's. That gives about 14-18 s per large binding per pass, roughly one whole-object size scan each (inference).
4. **Not a 1.0.1 regression, and specific to this data.** The same ~32-35 s request-2/3 tool time shows in the T03 gptr 1.0.0 batches (dev29, dev30). With gptr 1.0.0, T08 (lists of numeric peak matrices, about 8 GB) has only 1.7-2.75 s per-call gaps, and T01's request-2/3 A1 intervals are 1.15 and 4.61 s. So the cost is tied to T03's 1,231 data.tables, which hold about 224 M strings in 3 character columns (inference).
5. **Counterfactuals.** If each call's gap fell to C1's 0.67 s, A1's median would be 179.95 s, 20% below C1. Removing gptr's pre- and post-provider time as well gives 154.71 s, and matching C1's startup gives 150.22 s.

All of this is computed from published traces, with no new R timing runs, so other agents on this machine could not affect the numbers.

causes.title: Pre-gate risk classification plus permission gate on every r call whose code overwrites a large existing binding
causes.where: R/agent-dispatch.R:96 (call_risk via tool_call_hook), R/agent-dispatch.R:587-598 (perm_decide recomputes call_risk), R/perm-classify.R:2277-2299 (risk_binding_info -> risk_binding_leaf -> env_snap_size), R/utils-size.R:18 (env_snap_size); MCP entry R/mcp-server.R:73 and :191
causes.mechanism: The model's code always has a dead branch, `if (!exists("raw")) { files = ...; tables = ...; raw = ... }`. Static risk analysis treats those as overwrites of existing bindings and sizes each large one through env_snap_size. Classification runs once before the gate and again inside perm_decide. Trace data: the gap is 2.1-2.3 s when `raw` does not exist yet (request 1) and 28-36 s once it exists (requests 2 and 3). It roughly doubles to 55-57 s when the code also overwrites a second large binding (`tables`, A1-1). The single published replay splits it into 12.8-13.3 s before the gate and 13.4 s inside mcp_serve_gate.
causes.cost: Measured from traces (AWS, 2 vCPU, R 4.3.3). One large binding: 28.96, 29.90, 28.33, 36.02 s per call (median 29.4 s). Two bindings: 57.08 and 55.34 s. That is 88-96% of each call's outer time and 57.3-112.7 s of gap above C1's level per run. The gap is the same under gptr 1.0.0 (T03 dev29/dev30 request-2/3 tool time 30.1-35.8 s).
causes.safety_role: Risk classification flags writes, deletes, network use and overwrites of existing objects, and the gate enforces mode and rules on the final, post-hook input. Removing it would remove overwrite protection and the guarantee that approval applies to the hooked call.
causes.scales_with: Number of large existing bindings the code assigns, including in branches that never run, times the number of classification passes (2). Per binding it scales with object content: about 224 M strings costs ~14 s per pass, while T08's numeric matrices (1.0.0) cost <2.75 s per whole call.

causes.title: gptr time after the Codex provider returns in the request that creates the large object
causes.where: Between the usage event and request_end in A1 trace.jsonl (gptr_wait/peter run end). Mechanism not traced; candidate env snapshot with sizes at R/env-snapshot.R:120-171, called from R/ckpt-objects.R:464 and :547 (unverified)
causes.mechanism: After the CLI turn ends (usage event), gptr takes another 15-29 s before the request returns, but only in request 1, the request that creates `raw`. It doubles in A1-1 (29.4 s), which also kept `tables`. That points to one size or snapshot scan per new large binding at run end (inference). The benchmark counts it as harness/model/network time.
causes.cost: Measured, request 1: 29.40 s (A1-1, 2 bindings), 15.07 s (A1-2), 18.03 s (A1-3). Requests 2/3: 0.71-1.27 s. C1 analog (turn/completed to request_end): 0.023 s. Excess per run: 31.3, 17.0, 19.9 s (median 19.9 s).
causes.safety_role: Unknown from traces. Probably the end-of-run object ledger, checkpoint baseline or replay record that undo and session documents rely on.
causes.scales_with: Number of newly created large bindings in the run, and their content (strings).

causes.title: checkpoint_after in the request that creates raw
causes.where: internal elapsed of request-1 r call; R/ckpt-objects.R (object checkpoint policy, ~L458 per replay README)
causes.mechanism: Internal elapsed includes checkpoint_after. In request 1, A1's internal time minus input reading is 21.4-21.5 s (A1-2, A1-3), against 3.7-3.9 s of non-read R time in C1's request 1. The replay measured checkpoint_after at 13.865 s there and 0.08-0.15 s in requests 2/3. A1-1, with two bindings, has 35.7 s, about +14 s more.
causes.cost: Replay measured 13.9 s (single replay). In the original runs the excess over C1's R work is ~17.6 s in A1-2/A1-3 and ~31.9 s in A1-1; attributing it to checkpoint_after is inference.
causes.safety_role: Records which objects and files changed so undo can restore the pre-call state.
causes.scales_with: Size and content of newly added or modified bindings.

causes.title: gptr work before each Codex exec starts
causes.where: request_start to user message_end to provider start (usage.ts - seconds) in A1 trace
causes.mechanism: 1.0-3.4 s per request before `codex exec` is spawned: 2.8-3.0 s before the user message is even recorded in request 1, 1.6-1.7 s in request 2 and 0.85-1.07 s in request 3. C1's app-server takes 0.02 s from request start to turn/started.
causes.cost: Measured: 6.27, 6.70, 6.30 s per run (excess over C1 6.2-6.6 s).
causes.safety_role: Unknown from traces (run setup, prompt assembly, possible env baseline).
causes.scales_with: Decreases over requests 1 to 3 and is not tied to raw's presence. Unclear.

causes.title: A1 startup and cleanup outside requests
causes.where: biomedical/v0.5/aws/peter.R (benchmark driver: pkgload::load_all of gptr source, gptr_config, Matrix load)
causes.mechanism: A1's wall time includes R startup, load_all of the gptr source tree and session setup. C1 has app-server initialize plus thread start.
causes.cost: Measured: A1 5.52-5.65 s vs C1 1.02-1.36 s (excess about 4.5 s per run).
causes.safety_role: None (benchmark harness choice; an installed package would differ).

causes.title: checkpoint_before per call
causes.mechanism: Object, file and state capture before execution.
causes.cost: Replay measured 1.01 s (req 1), 1.44 s (req 2), 0.82 s (req 3); included in the gap above.

causes.title: Per-request Codex CLI process plus R MCP relay (A1 transport)
causes.where: R/cli-codex.R:1-9 (one `codex exec --json` per turn), R/cli-codex.R:45-54 (relay `Rscript --vanilla inst/gptr/mcp_relay.R`)
causes.mechanism: Every request spawns a new codex exec and an R relay process, and tool calls travel through the relay's mailbox. C1 uses one persistent app-server thread.
causes.cost: Not separable from model time. A1 time inside the provider minus tool outer is 74.3-81.9 s per run, versus C1 model/harness 74.1-86.3 s. Per request: req1 21.1-23.0 vs 21.0-26.2, req2 17.2-20.3 vs 17.5-19.3, req3 36.0-39.9 vs 35.6-40.8. No measurable penalty above noise.
causes.safety_role: gptr's hook in front of every tool, sandbox mapping (cli-codex.R:1-9).

measurements.what: T03 1.0.1: C1 per R command, Codex command span vs Rscript process time
measurements.result:
9 R commands: command span 40.49-56.88 s vs Rscript process 39.82-56.25 s.
- Overhead: median 0.67 s (0.63-0.78 s).
- Launch to R start: 0.19-0.22 s; R end to command end: 0.43-0.57 s.
- The wrapper call that launches R returns after 1.18-1.24 s (1 s yield), with R still running.
- Non-R, non-poll wrapper calls: median 0.11 s (0.09-0.71, n=6).
- Poll calls (write_stdin): median 5.03 s (n=51).
- Model turnaround before each poll: median 2.01 s (1.61-7.88).
- Latency from R finishing to Codex seeing it: 0.44-1.63 s per request.
- Codex wrapper time outside the Rscript process: 2.46-3.73 s per run.
- Tool counts: 19-28 inner calls and 19-25 outer exec wrappers per run, matching the benchmark's calls-by-tool.csv.
measurements.method: commandExecution item/started.startedAtMs and item/completed.completedAtMs from replay/C1-*/trace.jsonl app_server_event; Rscript start/finish from io.jsonl operation=rscript (recorded by io-bootstrap.R inside R); custom_tool_call and custom_tool_call_output emittedAtMs matched by call_id; inner tools counted by regex tools.<name>( in the exec input.

measurements.what: T03 1.0.1 per-request timing, median across 3 runs (s)
measurements.method: analyze_t03.py. The per-request split is exclusive. A1: read, then internal-minus-read (includes checkpoint_after), then outer-minus-internal, then the remainder. C1: read, then Rscript-minus-read, then wrapper time outside Rscript, then the remainder. C1 model time that overlaps Rscript stays hidden, as in the benchmark's convention.

measurements.what: T03 A1 request-2/3 tool time across gptr versions (benchmark request-stages tool_nonread_s, three trials each)
measurements.method: analyze_other.py over reports/T03/gptr-1.0.0-dev29, -dev30 and gptr-1.0.1 figures/request-stages.csv and all-attempts.csv.

measurements.result:
1. **Category asymmetry.** A1 tool_nonread is gptr's full outer interval, so gate, risk and checkpoint time count as tool time. C1 tool_nonread is only Rscript program time minus reads, so C1's launch/exit (0.67 s per call), wrapper, polling and detection latency fall into C1 harness/model time. A1 harness/model also includes gptr's own pre- and post-provider time (6.4 + 22.8 s mean).
2. **Transport differs.** A1 uses one `codex exec` per request plus an R MCP relay and its own instructions and tools (fewer tokens: input 308k vs 590k median, output 3.1k vs 4.3k). C1 uses a persistent app-server thread with code mode and 5 s polls.
3. **Execution conditions differ by design.** C1 must re-read inputs in finite Rscript processes; A1 is persistent.
4. **Different gptr versions per task.** T01, T08 and T03 dev29/30 used 1.0.0; T03 latest used 1.0.1. Benchmark versions also differ (dev.20/24/29/30), and A1 loads gptr with pkgload::load_all rather than an installed build.
5. **Agent-written code changes harness cost.** A1-1 kept `tables`, which doubled its gaps: the 322 s outlier comes from the code it wrote, not noise.
6. **Small, uncontrolled samples.** Three trials per arm, interleaved, OS cache not cleared, network and model latency uncontrolled, 2 vCPU host shared by the Codex CLI, relay and main R process, and A1 peak RSS 10.5-11.6 GiB on a 16 GiB host.
7. **Different runtime from local re-runs.** R 4.3.3 on AWS x86_64, versus the local R 4.6.1 arm64 any reproduction would use.
8. **Replay limits.** The published replay is a single offline-provider run of A1-2.
9. **T01 preload.** In T01 the A1 driver preloads input.rds before request 1, unlike T03, where the agent loads the data.
measurements.method: Source reading of the benchmark driver (aws/peter.R, aws/shared/execute.py), C1 app-server-client.jsonl thread/start params, gptr R/cli-codex.R:1-54, and the trace comparisons above.

open_questions: What runs in the 15-29 s between the provider returning (usage event) and request_end, only in request 1? Is it an end-of-run env snapshot with sizes (env-snapshot.R:120-171 via ckpt-objects.R:464/547), the replay recorder (GPTR_REPLAY=live), or something else? The published replay used an offline provider and did not time run end.

Is the ~14-18 s per-binding unit one env_snap_size walk over ~224 M strings (3 character columns x 60,664 rows x 1,231 tables)? Does it count shared sub-objects twice across bindings? A1-1's `tables` and `raw$tables` share the same data.tables, yet its cost doubled.

Does the T08 A1 code also contain the dead `if (!exists("raw"))` reassignment? Its tool inputs are not published. If it does, T08's 1.7-2.75 s gaps show the cost depends on content (strings), not on binding size in bytes.

gptr's object diff lists raw, files and other bindings assigned only in the dead branch as 'modified' in requests 2/3. Does checkpoint_before/after then snapshot them needlessly? Replay: 0.8-1.4 s before, 0.08-0.15 s after.
What is in A1's 0.9-3.4 s before-provider time? It falls from request 1 to 3 and does not depend on raw existing.
How much of A1's ~74-82 s per-run model+CLI+relay time is codex exec process startup plus relay R startup? It cannot be separated from the published traces.
